title: Winning is Futile
author: Brandon Moore
summary: This article argues that winning without the character-building struggle of losing fails to teach grit and resilience. Moore contends that many who achieve initial winning then quit at the first loss, lacking the education that struggle provides. The piece emphasizes that fathers should intentionally expose sons to work and struggle, creating opportunities for young men to experience aches and pains that come with building strength. The author suggests that winning alone doesn't develop the character that outlasts competition—hard work and pursuit of excellence do. Drawing on Christian faith, Moore argues that fathers should teach intentional self-improvement and that true winning comes not from achieving specific goals but from becoming better men than you were, a process that becomes the example you set for your sons.
points: Winning does not teach grit; it's losing, struggle, and the refusal to quit that provide the education needed to become a true winner. Fathers should invite boys into their struggles, stack wood together, and teach them through story and example how a man goes about the work of building character. True success comes not from winning against external competition but from becoming your best self and creating within your son the same striving toward excellence. Hard work builds character that outlasts any competition; help him craft the only man worthy of his competition—the ever-growing and learning version of himself. Real victory is becoming one of the fathers intentionally teaching and training his sons to be better men than he is.
quotes: Winning does not teach a man grit. It's the losing, the struggle, the refusal to quit that provides this education.
Who else is truly worthy enough to show him but you, his father.
Hard work will build the character that outlasts the competition provided by his peers.
You are meant to strive towards it with every breath of your being.
